text: The applicant is a Cypriot national of Turkish origin.
The applicant was born in 1950.
The applicant is a paediatrician.
The applicant resides in Nicosia, north of the "green line".
The applicant is a critic of the Turkish-Cypriot authorities.
The applicant is a critic of the Turkish military presence in the northern part of Cyprus, which he defines as "occupation".
The applicant is the "Turkish-Cypriot coordinator" of the Movement for an Independent and Federal Cyprus.
The Movement for an Independent and Federal Cyprus is an unregistered association of Turkish and Greek Cypriots.
The Movement for an Independent and Federal Cyprus was founded in 1989 in Nicosia.
The Movement for an Independent and Federal Cyprus has a Turkish-Cypriot coordinating committee in the northern part of Cyprus.
The Movement for an Independent and Federal Cyprus has a Greek-Cypriot coordinating committee in the southern part of Cyprus.
The purpose of the Movement for an Independent and Federal Cyprus is to develop close relations between the two communities (Turkish-Cypriot and Greek-Cypriot).
The Movement for an Independent and Federal Cyprus organises bi-communal meetings of a political, cultural, medical or social character.
The applicant is normally unable to obtain a permit from the Turkish and Turkish-Cypriot authorities to visit the "buffer-zone".
The applicant is normally unable to obtain a permit from the Turkish and Turkish-Cypriot authorities to visit the southern part of Cyprus in order to participate in various bi-communal meetings.

Between 8 March 1992 and 14 April 1998 (the date of the Commission's admissibility decision), only 6 out of 46 requests by the applicant for permits to visit the "buffer-zone" or the southern part of Cyprus were granted.
Between 18 April 1998 and 16 October 1999, two permit requests by the applicant were refused by the Turkish and Turkish-Cypriot authorities.
Of the two permit requests refused between 18 April 1998 and 16 October 1999, one was subsequently granted.
One of the refused permit requests concerned a UNFICYP (United Nations Peacekeeping Force in Cyprus) Spring Fair at Nicosia International Airport in May 1992.
One of the refused permit requests concerned a bi-communal medical seminar organised by the UNHCR (United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees) in June 1992.
One of the refused permit requests concerned a meeting of the coordinating committee for the Movement for an Independent and Federal Cyprus at the Ledra Palace in October 1992.
One of the refused permit requests concerned a meeting for the reorganisation of the coordinating committee of the Movement for an Independent and Federal Cyprus in April 1994.
One of the refused permit requests concerned a meeting for the reorganisation of the coordinating committee of the Movement for an Independent and Federal Cyprus in July 1994.
One of the refused permit requests concerned a seminar on cardiology organised by the UNHCR (United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees) in June 1994.
One of the refused permit requests concerned a general meeting of the New Cyprus Association in December 1997.
A number of the refused permit requests concerned receptions organised by the German embassy in Nicosia.
In May 1992, the Turkish and Turkish-Cypriot authorities refused to allow Greek Cypriots to attend a meeting organised by the applicant in the northern part of Cyprus.
The applicant claimed that the Council of Ministers of the "Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus" (the "TRNC") had adopted a decision prohibiting him from contacting Greek Cypriots.

Reference to the Council of Ministers of the "TRNC" decision prohibiting the applicant from contacting Greek Cypriots was allegedly made in a letter dated 3 February 1992 from the Health Minister of the "TRNC" to the applicant.

The letter dated 3 February 1992 from the Health Minister of the "TRNC" to the applicant stated: "According to the information our Ministry has received, you were informed by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Defence orally and this has been a decision of the government and we have nothing to add in our capacity as the Ministry."

On 7 May 1992, the applicant wrote to the Prime Minister of the "TRNC" requesting to be informed of the content of the Council of Ministers' decision referred to in the Health Minister's letter of 3 February 1992.
The applicant received no reply from the Prime Minister of the "TRNC" to his letter of 7 May 1992.
On 29 May 1992, the applicant sent a letter of protest to the Foreign Minister of Turkey.
The applicant's letter of protest of 29 May 1992 to the Foreign Minister of Turkey remained unanswered.

On 18 May 1994, the Directorate of Consular and Minority Affairs of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Defence of the "TRNC" informed the applicant that the permission requested by the applicant's letter of 19 April 1994 was refused for security reasons, in the public interest, and because the applicant had made propaganda against the State.

On 24 May 1994, the applicant wrote to the Deputy Prime Minister of the "TRNC" asking whether the previous decision of the Council of Ministers was still in force, since he was not allowed to visit the buffer-zone or cross over into Nicosia.
The applicant received no answer from the Deputy Prime Minister of the "TRNC" to his letter of 24 May 1994.
On 19 July 1994, the applicant sent a reminder to the Deputy Prime Minister of the "TRNC" regarding his letter of 24 May 1994.
The applicant's reminder of 19 July 1994 to the Deputy Prime Minister of the "TRNC" also remained unanswered.

The applicant claimed that in an article published in a newspaper on 18 March 1996, the former Deputy Prime Minister of the "TRNC" (to whom the applicant had sent the letters of 24 May 1994 and 19 July 1994) stated that when he had held the position of Deputy Prime Minister he had requested an explanation from the Prime Minister of the "TRNC" regarding the refusal of permits to the applicant.

The applicant claimed that in the newspaper article of 18 March 1996, the former Deputy Prime Minister of the "TRNC" stated that when he had held the position of Deputy Prime Minister he had requested an explanation from the President of the "TRNC" regarding the refusal of permits to the applicant, but had not received an answer.
